extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, research-integrity professionals, science journalists, and interested members of the public
extracted.subtask_description: A curated roundup of recent stories, investigations, and commentary about research integrity, retractions, peer review, AI in publishing, and related problems in academic publishing. The page highlights systemic problems and proposed/implicit standards for how journals, institutions, and the community should respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and timeliness of misconduct investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: “These investigations always take too long, are shrouded in secrecy, and lead to public statements crafted by attorneys and crisis consultants that are evasive and incomplete.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should be conducted more quickly and with greater transparency; public communications about findings should be candid rather than evasive or lawyer‑crafted boilerplate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting the published record to earn public confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: “[T]he scientific community writ large need[s] to redouble their commitment to conduct, communicate, critique, and—when an error is found, or misconduct detected—correct the published record in ways that both merit and earn public confidence.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When errors or misconduct are detected, corrections and retractions should be timely, clear, and designed to restore and maintain public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage honest (including negative) peer reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: “If we discourage negative reviews, positive ones will lose meaning.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review systems should allow and value critical negative assessments; discouraging negative reviews undermines the informative value of positive reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand access to peer review data
rubrics_metrics.description: “Journals must expand access to peer review data.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase transparency by making peer review reports, reviewer identities (when appropriate), and review histories more accessible to readers and watchdogs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use automated screening tools to detect paper-mill submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: “Up to one in seven submissions to hundreds of Wiley journals flagged by new paper mill tool.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals and publishers should adopt and deploy automated tools that screen submissions for paper‑mill patterns and other signs of systematic manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect potential integrity issues via automated bibliography analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: “Using automated analysis of the bibliography to detect potential research integrity issues.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ automated analysis of references and citation patterns as one method to surface suspicious or manipulated literature linkages for further human investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious about relying on citation metrics; watch for strategic manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: “Citation metrics and strategic mutations of scientific research: narratives and evidence.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that citation metrics can be gamed and may drive perverse incentives; evaluators should not treat raw metrics as sole indicators of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate reporting of research materials (e.g., cell line names)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Misspelled cell lines take on new lives — and why that’s bad for the scientific literature.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and journals must ensure accurate, precise reporting of materials and methods (including correct cell line identifiers) because small errors propagate and contaminate the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals should respond to data corrections and be receptive to whistleblowing
rubrics_metrics.description: “I sent my data to the original journal, and they didn’t care at all. It was very hard to get it published somewhere where you thought the reader of the original paper would find it.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals ought to take reports and submitted corrective data seriously, engage promptly, and make corrected information discoverable where readers of the original article will see it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect authorship integrity; avoid automatic or honorary authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: “Automatically listing senior members of departments as co-authors is highly prevalent in health sciences: meta-analysis of survey research.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship policies should prevent automatic inclusion of senior figures who did not meet authorship criteria; ensure authorship reflects actual contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose and manage AI-generated content and AI authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentions of an Elsevier paper written by ChatGPT going viral and report of “AI-generated rat genitalia” prompting publisher pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals and authors should have clear policies on disclosure of AI assistance, prohibit inappropriate AI authorship, and implement detection/oversight for AI‑generated or manipulated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactively debunk and retract flawed research
rubrics_metrics.description: “More published research should be debunked and retracted, watchdogs say.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The research community and journals should be willing to correct the literature by debunking and retracting invalid work, rather than allowing flawed studies to persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against predatory publishing and metric-driven incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion/interview excerpt suggesting many commercial publishers and predatory journals exploit academics and that output‑focused KPIs have led to overemphasis on quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions, funders, and researchers should be wary of predatory outlets and resist evaluation systems that reward volume over quality; reassess incentives and metrics used for hiring and promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider regulatory and inspection findings when evaluating published claims
rubrics_metrics.description: “‘Damning’ FDA inspection report undermines positive trial results of possible Alzheimer’s drug.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory inspection outcomes and compliance findings should inform the appraisal of clinical trial publications and may warrant reassessment or correction of published claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect researchers’ work from misattribution or misuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: researcher’s work published under the names of other researchers (Sara Farshchi’s case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers and institutions must safeguard proper attribution and guard against misappropriation or fraudulent republishing of others’ work.
